title: Consolidate diagnostic hooks and introduce low-overhead span relay
creator: Anika Patel
description: Consolidate the scattered diagnostic/tracing hooks across the runtime and introduce a low-overhead in-process 'span relay' responsible for batching, coalescing, and forwarding spans and diagnostic events to exporters. This reduces per-request allocations, minimizes lock contention in hot paths, and standardizes hook lifecycle across hosted/dedicated/private deployments. Scope: replace three divergent hook implementations in runtime/core, runtime/agent, and the sidecar shim with a single diagnostic-hook library + span-relay runtime component; add compatibility layer for existing exporters; provide gated rollout and metric-backed regressions tests.
acceptance_criteria: A single diagnostic-hook library is imported by runtime/core and agent; previous hook entrypoints are removed
Span relay reduces median span allocation per request by >= 60% compared to baseline
End-to-end tracing throughput (spans/s) increases without impacting 95th percentile latency of inference requests
Backward-compatible export: existing OTLP/Zipkin/Jaeger exporters work via the compatibility adapter
Canary rollout plan implemented in console with auto-fallback on error budget breach
Comprehensive unit + integration tests and a migration guide for partner exporters
tasks: Design: finalize lifecycle and API for diagnostic-hook library (contrib doc)
Implement: span-relay ring buffer and non-blocking flush worker
Adapter: build compatibility shim for current exporters
Refactor: replace old hook points in runtime/core and runtime/agent
Bench: microbenchmarks for allocs and latency across representative request sizes
E2E: canary deployment config and runbook for rollback
Docs: migration guide + Confluence design doc
perf_benchmarks: Baseline (main): median span allocs = 1,200 bytes, p95 latency overhead = +2.6ms
Post-relay (local perf run): median span allocs = 420 bytes (-65%), p95 latency overhead = +0.9ms
Throughput: 18% higher sustained exporter throughput in batch-forward mode during load tests
rollout_plan: Stage 1: feature-flagged in staging for all internal traffic (2d soak)
Stage 2: 10% of runtime-serving traffic via canary pool (48h, monitor error budget and latency SLOs)
Stage 3: 50% rollout if metrics stable, then 100% after 72 additional hours
Auto-fallback: console policy to revert to legacy hooks and exporters if error rate > 0.5% or 95th latency regression > 1.5ms
risks: Compatibility gaps with homegrown exporter extensions; mitigated by compatibility shim and adapter tests
Subtle ordering differences in span flush that could change trace structure; mitigated by integration tests and a strict comparison harness
Increased complexity in relay worker could introduce new resource usage patterns; mitigated by conservative defaults and throttling
